title: peg-constraint-backend: add PEG-based grammar backend, streaming framing, and tool-call enforcement
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Added a PEG-based constrained decoding backend with streaming-safe framing and improved tokenizer edge-case handling; OpenAI-compat tool-call enforcement now routes to structured-output backends with deterministic fallbacks.
description:
Context and motivation: We've seen recurring customer issues where grammar-style constraints (not easily expressed as regex or CFG fragments) require richer parsing semantics. Existing CFG and regex backends either fail on left-recursive/ambiguous constructs or produce unstable streaming boundaries when constraints span token edges. This PR introduces a PEG (Parsing Expression Grammar) constrained decoding backend designed for expressiveness, plus a streaming framing shim to avoid mid-token constraint violations during chunked streaming and to make tool/function-calling more deterministic.

What this change does: adds a new backend 'peg' to the constraint orchestration layer; implements a streaming-framing shim that ensures constraint checkpoints occur only at token-safe boundaries; integrates a post-decode verifier for tool/function calling outputs that maps PEG parse trees to the OpenAI-compat toolcall JSON schema; adds deterministic fallback logic to regex/CFG backends when the PEG grammar reports ambiguity or excessive backtracking. Includes unit and integration tests plus benchmark harness updates.

Key design notes: - PEG choice: we selected PEG over left-recursive CFGs to simplify runtime implementation (no need for generalized parsing) and to provide priorities inside grammars. Grammars are compiled into a compact DFA-like evaluator with backtracking limits to avoid OOM/latency spikes. - Streaming framing shim: streaming chunks are annotated with the last full-token index and constraint-state snapshot; partial token emissions are buffered until constraint-safe commit points. This avoids emitting fragments that violate grammar anchors mid-stream. - Tokenizer edge-case fixes: new logic to treat tokenizer subword anchors (e.g., 'Ġ', bytepair splits) consistently with grammar anchors; the PEG backend exposes a token-aligned anchor API so grammars can refer to byte boundaries or token boundaries explicitly. - Tool/function calling: added a verification layer that takes a PEG parse tree and serializes it into the OpenAI-compat toolcall envelope. If the tree does not conform to the expected signature, the router will attempt a deterministic fallback: 1) PEG grammar relaxed variant, 2) regex backend with post-check, 3) fail-safe empty toolcall with error metadata. This preserves caller semantics for clients relying on strict tool/json shapes.

Files changed (high level): - inference/constraints/peg_backend.py: new PEG evaluator, grammar compiler, backtracking guards. - inference/constraints/stream_framing.py: streaming-safe commit points and state snapshots. - api/openai_compat/toolcall_adapter.py: PEG-to-toolcall serializer and verifier. - runtime/constraint_orchestrator.py: routing logic + fallback policy config. - tests/constraints/test_peg_backend.py: unit tests exercising grammar constructs, backtracking limits. - tests/integration/test_streaming_toolcall.py: end-to-end streaming tests against OpenAI-compat client. - docs/constraints/peg_guide.md: usage guide and examples (anchoring, token-aligned grammars).

Commits (summary): - Add PEG grammar compiler and evaluator (with benchmarks) - Implement streaming framing shim and state snapshots - Wire up PEG backend into constraint orchestrator with policy flags - Implement PEG->OpenAI toolcall serialization and verification - Add unit/integration tests and test harness updates - Docs and example grammars + migration notes

Benchmarks and perf: Microbenchmarks show PEG backend adds ~4-8ms median overhead for constrained decoding on 2k-token histories vs regex backend but increases successful constraint satisfaction rates by ~18% on grammar-heavy workloads (large prompt sets used in internal evals). Streaming end-to-end tail latency improved by ~12% on constrained toolcall traces due to framing avoiding repeated fallback retries. Backtracking limits prevent pathological cases; we added counters and a new metric constraint.peg.backtracks to monitor occurrences.

Review summary and conversation: - Miguel Torres: "Overall design looks sound. Need to ensure backtracking limits are configurable by tenant and per-request." Author reply: "Agreed; exposed config in runtime/constraint_orchestrator with sane defaults and tenant overrides. Documented in peg_guide.md." - Eleni Vass: "Streaming shim seems complex — can we simplify by relying on prefix-KV cache markers?" Author reply: "Prefix-KV doesn't capture partial token emissions reliably across all tokenizers; the shim uses token-aligned indices and optional KV snapshots for widely-used models — added tests showing correctness." - Samir Gupta: "Please add more fuzz tests for ambiguous grammars to catch nondeterministic failures." Author reply: "Added fuzz harness and a deterministic seed for CI runs; also added metrics to detect non-determinism." - CI feedback: initial tests failed due to a race in state snapshot application (flaky integration test). Fix committed to ensure snapshot application is idempotent.

CI and gating: All CI runs passing after fix (unit tests, integration streaming tests, lint, type checks). Added long-running fuzz job scheduled nightly to monitor backtracking events.

Migration and configuration: The PEG backend is opt-in via runtime flag constraints.backend=peg. We recommend customers migrate grammars incrementally: start with a relaxed grammar and enable strictness once verified in staging. The default backtracking limit is 5000 operations; tenants can override via policy.

Fallback and safety: To avoid production regressions, the orchestrator will fall back to the regex backend when PEG reports either (a) backtracking limit exceeded, or (b) ambiguous parse detected on a strict grammar. All fallback events are logged and surfaced in the Redwood Console under Observability -> Constraint Events.

Docs and examples: docs/constraints/peg_guide.md contains grammar examples, token anchor patterns, and an example of producing a toolcall for function signature: {name:string, args:{}}. Also includes notes for OpenAI-compat clients about deterministic toolcall behavior.

Follow-ups and open items: - ENG-1168: Add tenant-level monitoring + alerting for frequent fallbacks. - ENG-1171: Evaluate JIT compilation for PEG evaluator to reduce overhead. - ENG-1190: Add migration helper tooling to convert common CFG snippets to PEG.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged into main; changelog entry prepared for the next patch release.
notes_for_release: Opt-in PEG constraint backend with streaming framing. Backtracking metrics added. No breaking changes to API; behavior may change for strict grammars when enabled.
test_plan: Run unit tests in tests/constraints and tests/integration; deploy to staging with constraints.backend=peg and run real traffic with Canary 5% for 48h; monitor constraint.peg.backtracks and Observability -> Constraint Events for fallbacks.
